items.title: How to choose the next safe step in application modernization
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[How to choose the next safe step in application modernization](https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/how-to-choose-the-next-safe-step-in-application-modernization/)** — _GitHub AI blog_. — Evidence-first modernization runbook: inventory what still works, then pick the least disruptive fix, shipped as the doc-and-modernize Copilot skill.
  - Decision order: keep, upgrade, swap, wrap, rewrite only with evidence
  - Safety levels L0–L4 state the strongest honest regression net
  - PiggyMetrics: Java 8 to Java 21, nine modules to seven

items.title: v1.7.0
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[v1.7.0](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/releases/tag/v1.7.0)** — _Pi releases_. — Pi 1.7.0 reopens your last session after a terminal restart, with its original profile, tool limits and instructions.
  - Image generation runs in codemode via Radius or OpenRouter image models
  - Copilot prompt cache survives thinking-level changes on Claude 5.x and GPT-6
  - Install telemetry removed, along with the PI_TELEMETRY setting

items.title: v2.4.2
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[v2.4.2](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/tag/v2.4.2)** — _OpenCode releases_. — GPT-6.2 Sol, Astra and the gpt-latest aliases now start from a system prompt written for GPT-6.2.
  - Esc on an empty composer returns your message, images included
  - Always allow on a web fetch now permits that site only
  - generate_image and generate_video move into Code Mode, about 700 tokens lighter

items.title: openclaw 2026.11.10
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[openclaw 2026.11.10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.11.10)** — _OpenClaw releases_. — 2026.11.10 turns Deep Research and browser handoff on by default, with ClawHub agent templates still behind Labs.
  - Deep Research is on by default and returns a cited report
  - Take control pauses agent clicks for 2FA prompts and CAPTCHAs
  - ClawHub agent templates stay off by default under Labs

items.title: v1.46.0
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[v1.46.0](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/releases/tag/v1.46.0)** — _OpenHands releases_. — OpenHands 1.46.0 adds team-org conversation unsharing, an in-app feedback flow, and a per-automation Git Sync switch.
  - Conversations shared with a team org can now be listed and unshared
  - Git Sync keeps an automation's activation status local

items.title: Inside the AI Training Data Market — Gabe Greenberg, G2i
items.bullet_md:
- 📝 **[Inside the AI Training Data Market — Gabe Greenberg, G2i](https://latent.space/p/inside_the_ai_training_data_market_gabe_greenberg_g2i/)** — _Latent Space (swyx)_. — G2i went from $15M to a projected $100M in training-data work without raising venture money.
  - Labs pay more for exclusive data, less if rivals can also buy it
  - Tasks must sit just ahead of the model; too hard and they become evals
  - Pilots cost frontier labs a few million dollars before any real order

items.title: Chinese and North Korean state hackers add ARTEX AI framework to their arsenal
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Chinese and North Korean state hackers add ARTEX AI framework to their arsenal](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/27/artex-ai-pentest-framework-china-north-korea-state-hackers/)** — _Help Net Security AI_. — Microsoft says ARTEX agents can go from a first scan to privileged access in minutes, not weeks.
  - The open-source tool appeared in July; its author pulled the code in October
  - Forks keep circulating, and ThreatBook now sells an ARTEX Pro build
  - One campaign logged 151,000 failed sign-ins, peaking at 2,900 a minute

items.title: Rumors swirling that labs might have cracked Factoring in P
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Rumors swirling that labs might have cracked Factoring in P](https://www.reddit.com/r/singularity/comments/1y59ef1/rumor_that_openai_or_anthropic_found_a_way_to/)** — _Hacker News (points)_. — Scott Aaronson says he is virtually certain AI labs hold cryptography results, though not what they are.
  - He says the RSA factoring rumour falls short of Factoring in P
  - A Google paper Wednesday adds a factoring algorithm with no practical break
  - OpenAI and Anthropic that week both published proofs of VP ≠ VNP

items.title: Anthropic wants to catch rogue AI activity without retaining your data
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Anthropic wants to catch rogue AI activity without retaining your data](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/25/anthropic-enterprise-frontier-safeguards-public-beta/)** — _Help Net Security AI_. — Anthropic's new beta spots misuse patterns across many requests while the conversation data stays in the customer's cloud.
  - Safety Cases hold findings but neither prompts nor responses, pulled via API
  - Older zero-retention checks judged each request in isolation
  - Live on Claude Platform, AWS and Google Cloud; Microsoft Foundry is next

items.title: Three studies from Meta and AMI Labs back Yann LeCun's bet on JEPA world models over large language models
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Three studies from Meta and AMI Labs back Yann LeCun's bet on JEPA world models over large language models](https://the-decoder.com/three-studies-from-meta-and-ami-labs-back-yann-lecuns-bet-on-jepa-world-models-over-large-language-models/)** — _The Decoder_. — LeCun's AMI Labs, which raised over $1 billion, published three JEPA studies covering separate pieces of the world-model bet.
  - Results span robot planning, more efficient training and error correction
  - They remain separate pieces, not yet one working system
  - The work also maps where physics still sets limits

items.title: 42 state AGs are trying to stop Character.AI from selling users’ chats
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[42 state AGs are trying to stop Character.AI from selling users’ chats](https://www.theverge.com/policy/1042620/character-ai-sale-state-ags-block-selling-users-chats)** — _The Verge AI_. — The Character.AI bankruptcy fire sale now has 42 attorneys general arguing over who gets to buy your old chats.
  - No buyer would have to honour privacy policies or delete chats on request
  - The lead bidder, Smirks and Pangs Acquisition, was incorporated November 13
  - New York, California and Colorado chatbot laws take effect January 1, 2027

items.title: AI data centers are becoming harder to build, and neoclouds are feeling it
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[AI data centers are becoming harder to build, and neoclouds are feeling it](https://techcrunch.com/podcast/ai-data-centers-are-becoming-harder-to-build-and-neoclouds-are-feeling-it/)** — _TechCrunch AI_. — Nvidia will not backstop a data center until it is nearly ready to run, and neoclouds are feeling the squeeze.
  - Construction delays and more expensive debt are hitting neoclouds
  - Land, power and a finished building matter more than a pitch deck
  - A 2027 shakeout could favour whoever can buy distressed projects

items.title: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
items.bullet_md:
- 🟢 **[GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities](https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-models-demonstrate-intrinsic-protein-design-capabilities)** — _OpenAI blog_. — OpenAI's GPT-6 models can now design protein shapes from a prompt and code, matching or beating specialist tools on most tasks.
  - 35 of 322 lab-made minibinders bound their target, a 10.9% hit rate
  - Motif scaffolding reached 43.7% versus 27.8% for RFdiffusion
  - Specialized models still supplied sequences and picked candidates for testing
  - Whole-structure prediction still lags: ESMFold2 averaged a 0.93 TM-score

items.title: Taking Trainium3 to the Track: Generating Videos with LTX-2.5
items.bullet_md:
- 🟡 **[Taking Trainium3 to the Track: Generating Videos with LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/blog/video-trainium3)** — _Hugging Face blog_. — A month on an AWS Trainium3 box ended with 10-second AI video clips generating in 22 to 23 seconds.
  - That is roughly the LTX API's 23.7 s, on half the machine
  - The first working attempt took 5 min 20 s at under half the resolution
  - Video decode alone dropped from 357 s to 1.6 s

items.title: Building on Nemotron 3.5 Parse: Open Data, Fine-Tuning, and Faster Inference
items.bullet_md:
- 🟡 **[Building on Nemotron 3.5 Parse: Open Data, Fine-Tuning, and Faster Inference](https://huggingface.co/blog/nvidia/building-on-nemotron-35-parse-open-data-fine-tunin)** — _Hugging Face blog_. — Nvidia is doing the Llama play for document readers: Parse 3.5 now ships with the data and fine-tuning recipe behind it.
  - Three open sets: 9.98M charts, 1M tables, 7.9M multilingual pages
  - SFT then RL took its development score from 66.24 to 71.38
  - DFlash2 drafting speeds decoding 7.62× at concurrency 1

items.title: Installing Linux & Windows with an LLM
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Installing Linux & Windows with an LLM](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eQg4OgSbKbI) — **Jim's Garage** (18m11s). — A demo of handing OS installs to a local model — for anyone curious how far agent control of hardware goes. - Hermes Agent drives a GL.iNet Comet X KVM through its web GUI and API - Ubuntu install runs from a single prompt - Jim flags it as a demonstration, not a production workflow

items.title: Stop Paying LLM Prices for Yes-or-No Answers — Chinmay Goyal, Glean
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Stop Paying LLM Prices for Yes-or-No Answers — Chinmay Goyal, Glean](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K5_ST-kMrvY) — **AI Engineer** (16m05s). — If you are paying generation prices for yes-or-no work, Glean's before-and-after numbers make the case for a decision model. - Expert routing at about 8x lower latency - Follow-up suggestions on time in 99.2% of cases, zero invalid outputs - Security-classifier recall up from 31.5% to 90.2%

items.title: Open Source LLM vs Claude API Cost, $1.60 vs $20 per Million Tokens
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Open Source LLM vs Claude API Cost, $1.60 vs $20 per Million Tokens](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gtHA2U6x3eU) — **GPU Battle** (2m26s). — Two minutes on what a rented 5090 actually costs per million tokens against the Claude Opus API. - About $1.60 per million generated tokens versus $20 for Opus 5.5 - Roughly 12x cheaper, with the caveat that it is not the same model - Prices and rentals move daily; benchmarks come from gpubattle.com

items.title: I fact checked a coding agent tier list
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [I fact checked a coding agent tier list](https://youtube.com/watch?v=AIcy5foM7zk) — **er1zav** (2m36s). — A two-minute sanity check on coding-agent tier lists: er1zav audits one creator's rankings claim by claim. - Covers Claude Code, Codex, Kiro, Antigravity and Pi - Starts with "Anthropic releases great models and then throttles them"

items.title: Claude Chat and Claude Code are becoming one app
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Claude Chat and Claude Code are becoming one app](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0g7_e0-jCLU) — **ICOR with Tom | AI Productivity** (6m23s). — Where Claude's app merge currently lands: projects in beta now surface inside Claude Code, with gaps on team plans. - Pinned projects appear in Code; team projects are not unlocked there yet - Nested sessions can mention each other for orchestration - New voice mode works in normal chat but not inside a project

items.title: Refact.ai – Open-Source AI Coding Agent, IDE Chat & Tool Integrations
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Refact.ai – Open-Source AI Coding Agent, IDE Chat & Tool Integrations](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QeudqT2XUSo) — **QUASA** (9m28s). — Configurable open-source coding agent for VS Code or JetBrains — repo-aware edits and command runs on your own model provider. - BSD-3-Clause license; hosted Refact Cloud and its plans have retired - Ships GitHub, Docker, database and MCP integrations - Local runtimes supported; the resident daemon is still an early preview - Scored 3.8/5, community support only

items.title: Gemini 4 Neon beat GPT-6.2 and Claude in my 25-task AI benchmark
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Gemini 4 Neon beat GPT-6.2 and Claude in my 25-task AI benchmark](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HnUtw3IWT3k) — **How I AI** (31m50s). — Six frontier models, 25 blind-scored tasks across coding, writing, video and prototyping — Gemini 4 Neon wins. - Field: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Neon and Carbon - Blends human blind scoring with LLM-as-judge ratings - Argues coding no longer separates the frontier models - Adds an Annoyance Bench built from her own agent sessions

items.title: Google Workspace MCP Servers Are Now Generally Available
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Google Workspace MCP Servers Are Now Generally Available](https://youtube.com/watch?v=EBFfUEGZC30) — **Outright Systems** (9m30s). — Google's hosted MCP servers now connect Gmail, Drive, Calendar and Sheets straight to Claude, with no third-party connector. - Setup runs through a Cloud project and an OAuth client for an AI agent - Form elicitation handles the user approvals - Ends with three real tasks against the connected apps - Rolling out to all Workspace customers over two weeks from Nov 24

items.title: Anthropic Just Changed the MCP vs CLI Fight
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Anthropic Just Changed the MCP vs CLI Fight](https://youtube.com/watch?v=2-G7X5I4t-4) — **The Hype Kevin** (10m31s). — MCP servers can now publish skills alongside their tools, loaded only when needed — a week after posts declared MCP dead. - Skills let a server take on longer, multi-step work while keeping context use low - Token cost of each approach measured on one GitHub task - Tool search has shipped in Claude Code since January - The catch, and which one to use for your setup

items.title: How to scan agent skills for security risks with Tessl
items.bullet_md: - 📝 **[How to scan agent skills for security risks with Tessl](https://tessl.io/blog/how-to-scan-agent-skills-for-security-risks-with-tessl)** — _Tessl blog_. — Walks through Tessl's Snyk-powered skill scanning — inventorying repo skills, failing CI on High or Critical findings, and setting install policies — starting from Snyk's 76 malicious payloads across 3,984 public skills.

items.title: How Clay Builds GTM Agents — Jeff Barg, Head of AI
items.bullet_md:
- 📝 **[How Clay Builds GTM Agents — Jeff Barg, Head of AI](https://latent.space/p/how-clay-builds-gtm-agents-jeff-barg-head-of-ai/)** — _Latent Space (swyx)_. — Clay's Jeff Barg rebuilt Sculptor as a coding agent on the Pi harness and puts qualifying all 40 million companies at about $1,500.
  - Usage is already near 50/50 between Clay's agent and outside harnesses like Claude Code
  - An automatic router ships soon because customers complain about the model selector

items.title: OpenAI may be in cost control mode
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[OpenAI may be in cost control mode](https://micjm.com/blog/openai-is-in-cost-control-mode/)** — _Hacker News (points)_. — micjm reads GPT-6.2's Astra and Sol as cost-tuned, with reasoning and output tokens per task down against matched opponents in its Agent Duel battles.
  - Output-token drop p-values: 0.0055 for Sol, 0.022 for Astra
  - Reasoning-token drop p-values: 0.00013 for Sol, 0.0064 for Astra
  - Astra 6 and Sol 6.1 look normal; the 6.2 pair are underthinking outliers

items.title: OS-Omni: Benchmarking Generalist Computer-Using Agents on Long-Horizon Workflows Across Platforms
items.bullet_md:
- 🧪 **[OS-Omni: Benchmarking Generalist Computer-Using Agents on Long-Horizon Workflows Across Platforms](https://huggingface.co/papers/2611.34232)** — _HF Daily Papers_. — OS-Omni is a live benchmark that runs computer-using agents on long-horizon workflows across six environments, including Windows, Ubuntu and mobile.
  - v1 has 48 tasks per platform plus 12 desktop-and-phone workflows
  - Tasks average 67.54 interaction steps, versus 15.0 for OSWorld
  - Claude Opus 5.5 leads at 68.5% success against a 77.3% human reference
  - Agents beat humans on Linux but trail by over 25 points on iOS and macOS

items.title: Google releases Cogentic papers on integer factorization, discrete logs and more
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Google releases Cogentic papers on integer factorization, discrete logs and more](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/master/cogentic_research_papers)** — _Hacker News (points)_. — Google Research posted six Cogentic-generated math papers in one commit, none peer-reviewed, with Lean formalizations promised later.
  - Headline claim is unconditional integer factorization in time L[1/3, 105]
  - Another claims Harary's 1964 edge-reconstruction conjecture for linear-density graphs
  - Cogentic runs on Gemini 4 from a problem statement with no expert hints
  - Google's repo says it is "not an official Google product"

items.title: Riemann proved with Claude, Jensen is BACK at Nvidia, is P vs NP next? & more AI news | ThursdAI Nov 26
items.bullet_md:
- 📝 **[Riemann proved with Claude, Jensen is BACK at Nvidia, is P vs NP next? & more AI news | ThursdAI Nov 26](https://sub.thursdai.news/p/the-riemann-hypothesis-has-a-proof)** — _ThursdAI_. — This week's roundup leads with a Lean-checked Riemann proof found with Claude and Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia.
  - Levent Alpöge's roughly 17 million-line Lean proof was certified by Lean and Mathlib maintainers
  - Anthropic and OpenAI published VP ≠ VNP proofs five hours apart, neither peer reviewed
  - Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang eleven days after he resigned
  - Thinking Machines open-sourced Inkling 2 Mini, a 26.4B looped transformer

items.title: DeepMind's Gemini agents discover quantum algorithms up to 290x cheaper, formally verified
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[DeepMind's Gemini agents discover quantum algorithms up to 290x cheaper, formally verified](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09822)** — _AlphaSignal · Nov 24_. — Teams of Gemini 4 agents cut resource costs across quantum algorithms, proving each result in Lean.
  - 290x faster arcsin routine; 2.57x speedup for an implementation of Grover's
  - Fusion simulation 11.8x cheaper, memory down from 5,650 to 4,338 qubits
  - Cytochrome P450 drug-metabolism simulation 2.5x cheaper, 481 to 333 qubits
  - Lean library, problem specs and verified solutions open-sourced on GitHub

items.title: MCP servers can now ship skills, run tasks, and more with Claude (6 minute read)
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[MCP servers can now ship skills, run tasks, and more with Claude (6 minute read)](https://claude.com/resources/articles/skills-over-mcp-tasks-and-more)** — _TLDR · Nov 26_. — Skills over MCP is in public beta, letting servers publish skills alongside their tools in Claude and Claude Code.
  - Tasks and Elicitation are now generally available
  - File Uploads, for PDFs, spreadsheets and images, is rolling out soon
  - Skills load only when needed and update with the server

items.title: Thinking Machines drops 26B open-source model that runs on 16GB RAM
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Thinking Machines drops 26B open-source model that runs on 16GB RAM](https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth)** — _AlphaSignal · Nov 23_. — Inkling 2 Mini is a 26.4B-parameter looped transformer with 3.4B active parameters.
  - Runs its middle layers three times per token; ~20GB native footprint
  - Scores 48.2% on DeepSWE v1.1, the maker's best under 100B parameters
  - Trained natively in NVFP4; GGUF builds ship via Unsloth and llama.cpp
  - Unsloth says the quantized build runs on 16GB RAM

items.title: Hardwood 1.1 Adds Parallel Parquet Writes, S3 Support, and ALP Encoding (7 minute read)
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Hardwood 1.1 Adds Parallel Parquet Writes, S3 Support, and ALP Encoding (7 minute read)](https://www.morling.dev/blog/s3-writes-parallel-encoding-alp-hardwood-1-1-0-cr1)** — _TLDR · Nov 26_. — Hardwood 1.1.0.CR1 closes the writer's two preview gaps: multithreaded encoding and direct S3 output.
  - Larger files stream to S3 as multipart uploads with up to four in flight
  - Row-group column chunks encode and compress in parallel, one thread per CPU
  - ALP cut test latitude and longitude columns 26% versus the default encoding

items.title: How Grab built Scarlet: the AI teammate that turns a Slack message into a production data pipeline (13 minute read)
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[How Grab built Scarlet: the AI teammate that turns a Slack message into a production data pipeline (13 minute read)](https://engineering.grab.com/how-grab-built-scarlet-blog)** — _TLDR · Nov 26_. — Grab rebuilt Scarlet around a skill library, adding data validation, per-user permissions and Jira/CLI entry points.
  - Prompt shrank about 25 times; team conventions now live in reviewed Markdown skills
  - Data checks post pass, fail or inconclusive, bound to the exact commit tested
  - Merge rate rose from about 50% in May to over 85% by September

items.title: OpenAI nine more AI-written math papers to GitHub, including a claimed proof that settles how fast computers can ever…

items.title: MAGI-2

items.title: The Rundown: Stanford and OpenAI physicist Venkatesa Chandrasekaran just an 83-page paper proposing a way to describe…
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[The Rundown: Stanford and OpenAI physicist Venkatesa Chandrasekaran just an 83-page paper proposing a way to describe…](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34924?_bhlid=d63f08ad2571f8d237cca197a5e4a971157964d4)** — _The Rundown AI · Nov 27_. — Stanford and OpenAI physicist Venkatesa Chandrasekaran posted an 83-page arXiv paper quantizing gravity in empty space, crediting GPT-6 Astra.

  - Claims finite answers, matching black hole entropy and low-energy Einstein equations
